findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered in a list without a `key`
findings.body: In the `rules.map(...)` loop the `'grafana'` branch now returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without passing `key={key}`, while the `'datasource'` and `default` branches still pass it. The component previously rendered (`GrafanaRuleLoader`) did receive the key. This produces React "Each child in a list should have a unique key" warnings and, because FilterView appends pages of results to the same array as the user scrolls, React will reconcile list items by index instead of identity – causing unnecessary unmounts/remounts and potentially showing stale rule content in the wrong row.

findings.title: Delete and Pause menu items can never render without a ruler rule, so they disappear from the ruler-less list view
findings.body: The menu still gates Delete on `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165) and Pause on `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123). After this change the Grafana rule list renders `RuleActionsButtons` with only `promRule` (see `GrafanaRuleListItem`), so `rulerRule` is always `undefined` there and both items are unconditionally hidden. The newly computed `grafanaDeleteAbility` / `grafanaPauseAbility` therefore have no effect (dead code), and users lose the ability to delete or pause a rule from the rule list – functionality that existed before this PR. The new test in `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` even asserts exactly 4 menu items with full permissions granted, codifying the loss of Delete/Pause.

findings.title: "Silence notifications" menu item is visible but does nothing when only a Prometheus rule is available
findings.body: `canSilence` in `AlertRuleMenu` is now also satisfied via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, so the "Silence notifications" item renders for rules in the list view where only `promRule` is passed. Clicking it calls `handleSilence`, which sets `showSilenceDrawer`, but the drawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true – `rule` (the ruler rule) is `undefined` in the list view. The result is a menu entry that silently does nothing. The silence drawer needs to be able to work from the Prometheus rule (uid/folder) or the item must be hidden.

findings.title: skipToken path still computes permissive abilities for a non-existent rule
findings.body: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` map `skipToken` to `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`, which does not short-circuit: with `rule === undefined`, `loading` is `false` (see `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`'s early return) and `isPluginProvided(undefined)` is `false`, so `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported` and `[AlertRuleAction.Duplicate] = [true, hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)]` (same for View/Explore). Since `AlertRuleMenu` OR-combines ruler and Grafana-prom abilities, a data-source (Mimir/Prometheus/Loki) rule – which always passes `skipToken` – will show "Duplicate" even when the ruler-based check says duplication is unsupported (e.g. ruler API unavailable, federated, plugin-provided rule), leading the user into a clone flow that cannot succeed. The skipToken/undefined case should return an all-`[false, false]` ability map.

findings.title: Federated rule-group immutability check dropped for CombinedRule abilities
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false` (the `isFederatedRuleGroup` import was removed). Previously the CombinedRule path computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which marked rules in Mimir federated groups (`source_tenants` set) as immutable and hid Edit/Delete/Duplicate. With this change the existing rule list/detail pages will offer Edit and Delete for federated rule groups; saving such a group through the UI editor can drop `source_tenants` and silently break cross-tenant federation. The federated check needs to be preserved (or re-derived from the group identifier) before merging.

findings.title: Grafana-managed recording rules lose Pause/Export/DeletePermanently support in the new ability hook
findings.body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` the supported flags for `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently` are derived from `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, i.e. alerting rules only. The ruler-based equivalent uses `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for Grafana-managed recording rules as well – those rules do support pausing and modify-export. Since the list view now relies exclusively on this hook, Export (and Pause, once the menu gating is fixed) will be missing for Grafana recording rules, a regression from the current list.

findings.title: OR-combining ruler and Prometheus abilities can override a deny, e.g. for provisioned rules
findings.body: All abilities are now computed as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (promSupported && promAllowed)`. Because a deny from the ruler-based check is ignored when the Prometheus-based check allows, any immutability signal that exists only in the ruler DTO is lost. Concretely, provisioning is detected in the prom path via `isProvisionedPromRule`, which reads the `provenance` field that is only now being added as an *optional* property on `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` (no backend change in this PR). If `/api/prometheus/grafana/api/v1/rules` does not return `provenance`, provisioned (file-provisioned/Terraform) rules will show Edit/Delete/Duplicate everywhere `promRule` is available – including the rule detail page where the ruler rule correctly reports the rule as immutable – and the subsequent write will be rejected by the API. Please confirm the API actually returns `provenance` and add a test with a provisioned rule; alternatively prefer the ruler result when it is available instead of OR-ing.

findings.title: Analytics `logWarning` is invoked from render and can be emitted repeatedly
findings.body: `getEditableIdentifier` is called during render and calls `logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier')` whenever neither a ruler rule nor a Grafana prom rule is supplied (e.g. a data-source Prometheus rule whose ruler rule has not loaded yet). Because this is a side effect in the render body it fires on every re-render of every such row, which can flood the analytics backend when a page contains many rules. Move the logging into an effect, or log once per identifier.

findings.title: `returnTo` query param dropped from rule view links
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` omits it, so navigating from the (filtered) rule list into a rule detail page loses the "return to previous" context and the user is no longer sent back to the list they came from.

findings.title: New Grafana-Prometheus ability logic has no unit tests
findings.body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`, the `skipToken` handling and the OR-combination in `AlertRuleMenu`/`RuleActionsButtons` introduce ~130 lines of new permission logic, but there are no tests for them: `RulesTable.test.tsx` mocks the whole `useAbilities` module (so the real logic never runs) and `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` only covers the happy path with all permissions granted plus a single "no update permission" case. Important cases are untested: provisioned rules (`provenance`), plugin-provided rules, recording rules, and `skipToken` (data-source rules) returning permissive abilities.

findings.title: Misleading test comment about skipToken behaviour
findings.body: The repeated comment "Cloud rules only need useRulerRuleAbilities mock (useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gets skipToken)" is incorrect: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` is still invoked with `skipToken` and, in production, still returns non-false abilities for some actions (see `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` with an undefined rule). The default `[false, false]` mock hides that behaviour, so the comment both misdescribes the code and conceals a gap in coverage for cloud rules.

findings.title: Stale comment and variable name after removing the ruler prefetch
findings.body: The ruler `prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)` dispatch was removed, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX ... doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded" and the variable is still called `cacheAndRulerPreload`. Both now describe behaviour that no longer exists and will mislead the next reader into thinking ruler data is still being warmed up here.
